Herminie Templeton Kavanagh, Darby O’Gill and the Good People.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/herminie-templeton-kavanagh/darby-ogill-and-the-good-people

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Herminie Templeton Kavanagh, the author, died 1933 (Wikidata Q15522437, date of death 1933-10-30).
- William Allingham, the writer of the preface, died 1889 (Wikidata Q261007, date of death 1889-11-18).

First publication of the text used: 1903 (SE colophon: 'Darby O’Gill and the Good People was published in 1903 by Herminie Templeton Kavanagh.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1903, before 1931. The edition's own statement of rights, quoted below, says the text is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin: the possible countries of first publication are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Nothing in the facts points to France, Spain, Mexico, Colombia or Russia/USSR. The last person to die among those named above died in 1933, and each of these countries has a term of life + 70 years or less, so the work is public domain in each of them.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: first publication 1903 (quoted above).
- Wikidata Q15522437 (Herminie Templeton Kavanagh), P570 = 1933-10-30.
- Wikidata Q261007 (William Allingham), P570 = 1889-11-18.
